shared_elements: frontal human head carved in the round on a block/pillar
browridge rendered as a continuous raised horizontal ridge over both eyes
recessed almond/slit eyes beneath the ridge
vertical nose joined to the browridge in a T-shape
mouth rendered as a small horizontal element low on the face
undecorated flat cranium/upper block above the face
face occupying lower portion of a tapering columnar mass
justification: Both depict a schematic frontal human head sculpted from a columnar block, with the highly distinctive convention of a single continuous raised brow ridge running across the whole face and merging with a straight vertical nose to form a T, deep-set slit eyes tucked beneath it, and a plain flat-topped cranium above; the mouth is a small horizontal feature set low. Differences are minor and mostly in condition and detail (A shows an oval, more clearly cut lips and a rounder cheek line, B has a broader block with more angular flanking masses and a heavily lost lower face), not in the iconographic scheme.
